questions.questionText: One of the roots of the equation x2 - 12x + k = 0 is x = 3. The other root is _______.
questions.questionTextHi: समीकरण x2 - 12x + k = 0 का एक मूल x = 3 है। दूसरा मूल _______ है।
questions.explanation:
**Given:**

One of the roots of the equation x2 - 12x + k = 0 is x = 3.

**Concept Used:**

If one root of a quadratic equation ax2 + bx + c = 0 is α, then the other root β can be found using the relationship:

Sum of roots = -b/a

Product of roots = c/a

**Calculation:**

Given the equation: x2 - 12x + k = 0

One root (α) = 3

Using the sum of roots formula:

⇒ α + β = -(-12)/1

⇒ 3 + β = 12

⇒ β = 12 - 3

⇒ β = 9

**∴ The other root is 9.**
questions.explanationHi:
**दिया गया है:**

समीकरण x2 - 12x + k = 0 का एक मूल x = 3 है।

**प्रयुक्त अवधारणा:**

यदि द्विघात समीकरण ax2 + bx + c = 0 का एक मूल α है, तो दूसरा मूल β निम्न सम्बन्ध का उपयोग करके ज्ञात किया जा सकता है:

मूलों का योग = -b/a

मूलों का गुणनफल = c/a

**गणना:**

दिया गया समीकरण: x 2 - 12x + k = 0

एक मूल (α) = 3

मूलों के योग सूत्र का उपयोग:

⇒ α + β = -(-12)/1

⇒ 3 + β = 12

⇒ β = 12 - 3

⇒ β = 9

**∴ दूसरा मूल 9 है।**

questions.questionText: Anil sells a table to Kamal at a profit of 10% and Kamal sells it to Rajat at a profit of 12%. If Rajat pays ₹ 246.40 for it, then how much had Anil paid for it?
questions.questionTextHi: अनिल एक मेज को 10% लाभ पर कमल को बेचता है और कमल 12% लाभ पर इसे रजत को बेचता है। यदि रजत इसके लिये ₹ 246.40 का भुगतान करता है, तो अनिल ने कितना भुगतान किया होगा?
questions.explanation:
**Formula Used:**

X% = X/100

**Calculation:**

Let price paid by Anil = 100 unit

Anil sells it to Kamal at 10% profit

⇒ Costprice for Kamal = 100 × 110% = 100 ×\( \frac{110}{100} \) = 110 unit

Kamal sells it to Rajat at 12% profit

⇒ Costprice for Rajat = 110 × 112% = 110 ×\( \frac{112}{100} \) = 123.2 unit

Rajat pays ₹ 246.40 for table 

⇒ 123.2 unit = ₹ 246.40

⇒ 1 unit = 246.4/123.2 = ₹ 2

⇒ 100 unit = 100 × 2 =  ₹ 200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 200**
questions.explanationHi:
**प्रयुक्त सूत्र:**

X% = X/100

**गणना:**

माना अनिल द्वारा भुगतान किया गया मूल्य = 100 इकाई

अनिल इसे कमल को 10% लाभ पर बेचता है। 

⇒ कमल के लिए क्रय मूल्य = 100 × 110% = 100 ×\( \frac{110}{100} \) = 110 इकाई

कमल इसे रजत को 12% लाभ पर बेचता है। 

⇒ रजत के लिए क्रय मूल्य = 110 × 112% = 110 ×\( \frac{112}{100} \) = 123.2 इकाई

रजत मेज के लिए ₹ 246.40 का भुगतान करता है। 

⇒ 123.2 इकाई = ₹ 246.40

⇒ 1 इकाई = 246.4/123.2 = ₹ 2

⇒ 100 इकाई = 100 × 2 =  ₹ 200

**∴ सही उत्तर ₹200 है। **

questions.questionText: The cost of painting a spherical vessel of diameter 14 cm is Rs. 21,560. What is the cost of painting (in Rs.) per square centimetre? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.questionTextHi: 14 cm व्यास वाले एक गोलाकार बर्तन को पेंट करने की लागत 21,560 रुपये है। प्रति वर्ग सेंटीमीटर पेंटिंग की लागत (रुपये में) कितनी है? (π = 22/7 का उपयोग कीजिए)
questions.explanation:
**Given:**

The cost of painting a spherical vessel of diameter 14 cm is Rs. 21,560.

**Concept:**

To find the cost of painting per square centimetre, we need to determine the surface area of the sphere and then divide the total cost by this surface area.

**Formula Used:**

Surface area of a sphere = 4πr2

Cost per square centimetre = Total cost / Surface area

**Calculation:**

We have,

Diameter = 14 cm

⇒ Radius (r) = Diameter / 2 = 14 cm / 2 = 7 cm

Surface area of the sphere = 4πr2

⇒ Surface area = 4 × (22/7) × 72

⇒ Surface area = 4 × (22/7) × 49

⇒ Surface area = 4 × 22 × 7

⇒ Surface area = 616 cm2

Cost per square centimetre = Total cost / Surface area

⇒ Cost per square centimetre = 21560 / 616

⇒ Cost per square centimetre ≈ 35 Rs/cm2

**∴ The cost of painting per square centimetre is Rs. 35**
questions.explanationHi:
**दिया गया है:**

14 cm व्यास वाले एक गोलाकार बर्तन को पेंट करने की लागत 21,560 रुपये है।

**प्रयुक्त अवधारणा:**

प्रति वर्ग सेंटीमीटर पेंटिंग की लागत ज्ञात करने के लिए, हमें गोले के पृष्ठीय क्षेत्रफल को निर्धारित करने की आवश्यकता है और फिर इस पृष्ठीय क्षेत्रफल से कुल लागत को विभाजित करना होगा।

**प्रयुक्त सूत्र:**

गोले का पृष्ठीय क्षेत्रफल = 4πr2

प्रति वर्ग सेंटीमीटर लागत = कुल लागत / पृष्ठीय क्षेत्रफल

**गणना:**

हमारे पास है,

व्यास = 14 cm

⇒ त्रिज्या (r) = व्यास / 2 = 14 cm / 2 = 7 cm

गोले का पृष्ठीय क्षेत्रफल = 4πr2

⇒ पृष्ठीय क्षेत्रफल = 4 x (22/7) x 72

⇒ पृष्ठीय क्षेत्रफल = 4 x (22/7) x 49

⇒ पृष्ठीय क्षेत्रफल = 4 x 22 x 7

⇒ पृष्ठीय क्षेत्रफल = 616 cm2

प्रति वर्ग सेंटीमीटर लागत = कुल लागत / पृष्ठीय क्षेत्रफल

⇒ प्रति वर्ग सेंटीमीटर लागत = 21560 / 616

⇒ प्रति वर्ग सेंटीमीटर लागत ≈ 35 रुपये/cm2

**∴ प्रति वर्ग सेंटीमीटर पेंटिंग की लागत 35 रुपये है।**

questions.questionText: At his usual speed of 48 km/hr, a man reaches his office in time. If he goes by 5/6 of his usual speed, he will reach his office 8 minutes late. What is the distance to his office from home?
questions.questionTextHi: 48 किमी/घंटा की अपनी सामान्य गति से, एक आदमी समय पर अपने कार्यालय पहुंचता है। यदि वह अपनी सामान्य गति की 5/6 गति से जाता है, तो वह अपने कार्यालय 8 मिनट देरी से पहुंचेगा। घर से उसके कार्यालय की दूरी क्या है?
questions.explanation:
**Given:**

Usual speed of the man = 48 km/hr

Reduced speed = (5/6) × 48 km/hr

Time difference = 8 minutes = 8/60 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Let the usual time taken to reach the office be t hours.

Distance = Usual speed × Usual time

Distance = 48 × t

At reduced speed, the time taken = t + 8/60 hours

Distance = Reduced speed × (t + 8/60)

Distance = (5/6) × 48 × (t + 8/60)

Since the distance is the same, we equate the two expressions:

48 × t = (5/6) × 48 × (t + 8/60)

Simplify the equation:

48t = 40 (t + 8/60)

⇒ 48t = 40t + 40 × 8/60

⇒ 48t = 40t + 40 × 8/60

⇒ 48t - 40t = 40 × 8/60

⇒ 8t = 40 × 8/60

⇒ 8t = 40 × (4/30)

⇒ 8t = 40/7.5

⇒ 8t = 40/7.5

⇒ 8t = 5.3333

⇒ t = 5.3333 / 8

⇒ t = 0.6666 hours

Distance = 48 × 0.6666

Distance = 32 km

**The distance to his office from home is 32 km.**
questions.explanationHi:
**दिया गया है:**

आदमी की सामान्य गति = 48 किमी/घंटा

कम हुई गति = (5/6) × 48 किमी/घंटा

समय का अंतर = 8 मिनट = 8/60 घंटे

**प्रयुक्त सूत्र:**

दूरी = गति × समय

**गणना:**

मान लीजिए कि कार्यालय तक पहुँचने में लगने वाला सामान्य समय t घंटे है।

दूरी = सामान्य गति × सामान्य समय

दूरी = 48 × t

कम हुई गति से, लगने वाला समय = t + 8/60 घंटे

दूरी = कम हुई गति × (t + 8/60)

दूरी = (5/6) × 48 × (t + 8/60)

चूँकि दूरी समान है, हम दोनों व्यंजकों को समान करते हैं:

48 × t = (5/6) × 48 × (t + 8/60)

समीकरण को सरल करें:

48t = 40 (t + 8/60)

⇒ 48t = 40t + 40 × 8/60

⇒ 48t = 40t + 40 × 8/60

⇒ 48t - 40t = 40 × 8/60

⇒ 8t = 40 × 8/60

⇒ 8t = 40 × (4/30)

⇒ 8t = 40/7.5

⇒ 8t = 40/7.5

⇒ 8t = 5.3333

⇒ t = 5.3333 / 8

⇒ t = 0.6666 घंटे

दूरी = 48 × 0.6666

दूरी = 32 किमी

**उसके घर से कार्यालय की दूरी 32 किमी है।**

questions.questionText: Raghu and Raman start together to walk a certain equal distance at a speed of 10 km/h and 8 km/h, respectively. Raghu arrives 30 minutes before Raman arrives. Find the distance between the start and the end point.
questions.questionTextHi: रघु और रमन एक निश्चित समान दूरी को क्रमशः 10 किमी/घंटा और 8 किमी/घंटा की गति से तय करना प्रारंभ करते हैं। रमन के पहुँचने के 30 मिनट पहले रघु पहुँचता है। तो प्रारंभिक और समाप्ति बिंदु के बीच की दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.explanation:
Given:

Speed of Raghu = 10 km/h

Speed of Raman = 8 km/h

Difference of time taken by Raghu and Raman = 30 minutes

Concept:

Speed is inversely proportional to time. 

Formula Used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculation:

As per question,

We take the 1st case (any case could be taken for solution, answer will be same as distance is same in both the cases)

 Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ (10 × 8) units

⇒ 80 units

⇒ 1 unit = (1/4) hours

⇒ 80 units = 80 × (1/4) 

⇒ 20 Km

∴ The distance between the start and the end point is 20 km.

**Mistake Points**  This method is used when distance is equal in both the cases.

**Alternate Method**Given:

Speed of Raghu = 10 km/h

Speed of Raman = 8 km/h

Difference of time taken by Raghu and Raman = 30 minutes

Formula Used:

Time= Distance/Speed

Calculation:

Let the distance be D km/h

According to question,

(D/8) - (D/10) = 30 minutes

⇒ (30/60) hours

⇒ (1/2) hours

⇒ (5D - 4D)/40 = 1/2

D = 20 km

**∴ The distance between the start and the end point is 20 km.**
questions.explanationHi:
दिया गया है:

रघु की गति = 10 किमी/घंटा

**Given:**

The area of a rectangular park is 10,560 m2.

The sum of its one diagonal and the shorter side is 2.2 times its longer side.

**Concept used:**

Area of a rectangle = l × b

Diagonal of a rectangle = √(l2 + b2)

Perimeter of a rectangle = 2(l + b)

Perimeter of a square = 4a

Diagonal of square = a√2

Here,

l = length of the rectangle

b = breadth of the rectangle

a = side of the square

**Calculation:**

Let the length and breadth of the rectangle be L and B

So, diagonal = √(L2 + B2) + B = 2.2L

⇒ L2 + B2 + B2 + 2.B.√(L2 + B2) = 4.84L2

⇒ 2B2 + 2.B.√(L2 + B2) = 4.84L2 - L2

⇒ 2B[B + √(L2 + B2)] = 3.84L2

⇒ 2B × 2.2L = 3.84L2

⇒ 4.4B = 3.84L

⇒ B/L = 3.84/4.4 = 48/55

So, ratio of B and L = 48 : 55

Let L and B be 55x and 48x

Now,

55x × 48x = 10560

⇒ x2 = 10560/2640

⇒ x2 = 4

⇒ x = 2

So, length and breadth = 55 × 2 = 110 m, 48 × 2 = 96 m

Now,

Perimeter of the rectangle = 2(110 + 96)

⇒ 2 × 206 = 412 m

So, the perimeter of the square = 412 - 12

⇒ 400 m

So, side of the square = 400/4 = 100 m

Diagonal = 100√2 m

**∴ The length (in m) of each diagonal of the square field is 100√2.**

questions.questionText: 44 pipes can fill a large water tank in 27 hours. How many hours will it take for 66 pipes to fill four such tanks?
questions.questionTextHi: 44 नल एक बड़ी टंकी को 27 घंटे में भर सकते हैं। ऐसी चार टंकियों को भरने में 66 नलों को कितने घंटे लगेंगे?
questions.explanation:
Shortcut Trick
Using the chain rule formula: M1 × H1 / W1 = M2 × H2 / W2

⇒ 44 × 27 / 1 = 66 × H2 / 4

⇒ H2 = (44 × 27 × 4) ÷ 66

⇒ H2 = 72

**∴ The correct answer is 72 hours.**

**Alternate Method**

**Given:**

Initial number of pipes (M1) = 44

Time to fill 1 tank (H1) = 27 hours

New number of pipes (M2) = 66

Number of tanks to fill (W2) = 4

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken by 44 pipes to fill 1 tank = 27 hours

⇒ Total time taken by 1 pipe to fill 1 tank = 44 × 27 = 1188 hours

⇒ Time taken by 66 pipes to fill 1 tank = 1188 ÷ 66 = 18 hours

⇒ Time taken by 66 pipes to fill 4 such tanks = 18 × 4 = 72 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 72 hours.**

**Additional Information**

Unitary Method in Time & Work

If more resources (pipes) are used, less time is taken to do the same amount of work (Inverse Proportion). If more work (tanks) is done, more time is taken (Direct Proportion).

MDH Formula

A direct shortcut to compare two scenarios of work: (M1 × D1 × H1) ÷ W1 = (M2 × D2 × H2) ÷ W2, where M is workers or identical machines, and W is the total work done.

Pipes & Cisterns

All pipes of identical size fill a tank at the exact same rate. Their combined efficiency is directly proportional to the total number of active pipes.

⇒ H2 = (44 x 27 x 4) ÷ 66

⇒ H2 = 72

questions.questionText: Vijay sells bananas at the rate of Rs. 13 per dozen and earns a profit of 30 percent. The cost price of the bananas increases by 10 percent. If the selling price remains the same, then what is his new profit percent?

questions.explanation:
Shortcut Trick
Let the initial Cost Price (CP) be 100 units.

Since the initial profit is 30%, Selling Price (SP) = 130 units.

The new CP increases by 10%, so New CP = 110 units.

Since the SP remains the same (130 units), New Profit = 130 − 110 = 20 units.

New Profit % = (20 ÷ 110) × 100 = 18.18%.

**∴ The correct answer is 18.18%.**

**Alternate Method**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) of bananas = Rs. 13 per dozen

Initial Profit = 30%

Cost Price increases by 10% and SP remains the same.

**Formula Used:**

CP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 + Profit%)

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial CP = (13 × 100) ÷ (100 + 30)

⇒ Initial CP = 1300 ÷ 130 = Rs. 10

⇒ New CP = Initial CP + 10% of Initial CP

⇒ New CP = 10 + (10 ÷ 100) × 10 = Rs. 11

⇒ The Selling Price remains the same, so New SP = Rs. 13

⇒ New Profit = New SP − New CP = 13 − 11 = Rs. 2

⇒ New Profit % = (New Profit ÷ New CP) × 100

⇒ New Profit % = (2 ÷ 11) × 100 = 18.18%

**∴ The correct answer is 18.18%.**

**Additional Information**

Marked Price (MP) and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price. Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount. Furthermore, Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given on an article, Effective Single Discount = a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer Trick

If a dealer sells goods at CP but uses a false weight, his Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.

questions.explanation:
**Given:**

A person travels at the speed of 12 kmph, 14 kmph, and 6 kmph on the surface of an equatorial triangular plane.

**​Concept used:**

Distance = Speed x Time 

Average speed = \(\frac{Total \ distance}{Total \ time}\)

**Calculation:**

Let the side of each equilateral plane be x km

Now,

Time is taken to cover x km distance with a speed of 12 kmph = \(\frac{x}{12}\) hr.

Time is taken to cover x km distance with a speed of 14 kmph = \(\frac{x}{14}\) hr.

questions.explanation:
Given: 

A can do a piece of work in 10 days while B can do the same work in 20 days.

They start together but A leaves after three days.

Calculation:

The time taken by A to complete the piece of work = 10 days

The efficiency of A \(= \frac{1}{10}\)

The time taken by B to complete the piece of work = 20 days

The efficiency of B \(= \frac{1}{20}\)

The combined efficiency of A and B or the amount of work done in one day \(= \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{20} = \frac{3}{20} \)

Since they start together but A leaves after three days,

Therefore,

The amount of work done in three days \(= 3 \times \frac{3}{20} = \frac{9}{20} \)

The remaining work \(=1 - \frac{9}{20} = \frac{11}{20} \)

Since the efficiency of B is \( \frac{1}{20}\),

Therefore, the required number days to complete the remaining work by B \(= \frac{\frac{11}{20}}{\frac{1}{20}} = 11 \text { days }\)

∴** In 11 days B complete the remaining work.**

**Given:**

Three solid spheres of diameters 6 cm, 8 cm, and 10 cm are melted to form a single solid sphere.

**Formula used:**

Volume of a sphere = \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\)

The volume of the resulting sphere is equal to the sum of the volumes of the three smaller spheres.

**Calculation:**

Radius of the first sphere, r1 = 6/2 = 3 cm

Radius of the second sphere, r2 = 8/2 = 4 cm

Radius of the third sphere, r3 = 10/2 = 5 cm

Volume of the resulting sphere = volume of first sphere + volume of second sphere + volume of third sphere

⇒ \(\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3\) = 4⁄3π(33) + 4⁄3π(43) + 4⁄3π(53)

⇒ R3 = 33 + 43 + 53

⇒ R3 = 27 + 64 + 125

⇒ R3 = 216

⇒ R = 6 cm

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

Shortcut Trick
The given mathematical expression directly matches an algebraic identity.

x2 + y2 + z2 − 2xy − 2xz + 2yz = (x − y − z)2

Substitute the given variable values into the term (x − y − z):

⇒ (b + c) − (c − a) − (a − b) = b + c − c + a − a + b = 2b

⇒ (2b)2 = 4b2

**∴ The correct answer is 4b2.**

**Alternate Method**

**Given:**

⇒ x = b + c

⇒ y = c − a

⇒ z = a − b

**Formula Used:**

⇒ (p + q + r)2 = p2 + q2 + r2 + 2pq + 2qr + 2pr

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let us evaluate the given expression: x2 + y2 + z2 − 2xy − 2xz + 2yz

⇒ Comparing this with our standard formula, we take p = x, q = −y, and r = −z.

⇒ This simplifies our original expression cleanly to: (x − y − z)2

⇒ Next, we substitute the given expressions for x, y, and z into (x − y − z):

⇒ x − y − z = (b + c) − (c − a) − (a − b)

⇒ Distribute the negative signs and open the brackets:

⇒ x − y − z = b + c − c + a − a + b

⇒ Cancel out the opposite terms (+c − c) and (+a − a) and group together:

⇒ x − y − z = 2b

⇒ Finally, substitute this result back into the squared identity expression:

⇒ (x − y − z)2 = (2b)2 = 4b2

**∴ The correct answer is 4b2.**

**Additional Information**

Trinomial Expansion Identity

The fundamental identity for the square of a sum of three variables is represented as (a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca.

By assigning negative signs to the variables, we derive adapted identities depending on the requirements. For instance, (a − b − c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 − 2ab + 2bc − 2ca.

questions.questionTextHi: एक पंसारी ने 40 रुपये प्रति किलोग्राम की दर से 50 किलोग्राम चीनी खरीदी और उसे 30 रुपये प्रति किलोग्राम की दर से 70 किलोग्राम चीनी के साथ मिलाया। 20% लाभ अर्जित करने के लिए उसे मिश्रण (प्रति किलोग्राम) किस दर पर बेचना चाहिए?
questions.explanation:
**Given:**

Cost price of 50 kg sugar at Rs. 40/kg = 50 × 40.

Cost price of 70 kg sugar at Rs. 30/kg = 70 × 30.

Total weight of sugar = 50 kg + 70 kg.

Gain = 20%.

**Formula Used:**

Total Cost Price = Sum of the cost prices of both types of sugar.

Selling Price = Total Cost Price + Gain% of Total Cost Price.

**Calculation:**

Cost price of 50 kg sugar = 50 × 40 = Rs. 2000.

Cost price of 70 kg sugar = 70 × 30 = Rs. 2100.

Total Cost Price = 2000 + 2100 = Rs. 4100.

Total weight of sugar = 50 kg + 70 kg = 120 kg.

Gain = 20% of 4100 = (20/100) × 4100 = Rs. 820.

Selling Price = Total Cost Price + Gain = 4100 + 820 = Rs. 4920.

Rate of selling per kg = Selling Price / Total weight = 4920 / 120.

Rate of selling per kg = Rs. 41.

**The rate at which he should sell the mixture per kg to gain 20% is Rs. 41.**

Mode = 3median - 2 mean

questions.questionText: The average marks obtained by a group of students in a Mathematics test was 72. The average marks of the male students were 60, while that of the female students were 80. What was the ratio of the number of male students to the number of female students in that group?
questions.questionTextHi: गणित की परीक्षा में छात्रों के एक समूह द्वारा प्राप्त औसत अंक 72 थे। लड़कों के औसत अंक 60 थे, जबकि लड़कियों के औसत अंक 80 थे। उस समूह में लड़कों की संख्या और लड़कियों की संख्या का अनुपात कितना था?
questions.explanation:
**Given:**

Average marks of all students is 72.

Average marks of male students is 60 and females students is 80.

**Calculations:**

Let the number of boys be x and girls be y

According to problem,

60x + 80y = 72(x + y)

=> 60x + 80y = 72x + 72y

=> 80y - 72y = 72x - 60x

=> 8y = 12x

=> x : y = 2 : 3

**∴ The answer is 2 : 3**
questions.explanationHi:
**दिया गया है:**

सभी छात्रों के औसत अंक 72 हैं।

लड़कों के औसत अंक 60 और लड़कियों के औसत अंक 80 हैं।

**गणना:**

माना लड़कों की संख्या x और लड़कियों की संख्या y है।

प्रश्नानुसार,

60x + 80y = 72(x + y)

=> 60x + 80y = 72x + 72y

=> 80y - 72y = 72x - 60x

=> 8y = 12x

=> x : y = 2 : 3

**∴ सही उत्तर 2 : 3 है।**

questions.questionText: Rajesh needs to buy some cardboard to build a box that is 12 inches long, 8 inches wide, and 10 inches high. How much cardboard is needed to build the box?
questions.questionTextHi: राजेश को 12 इंच लंबाई, 8 इंच चौड़ाई और 10 इंच ऊँचाई वाले एक बॉक्स बनाने के लिए कुछ गत्ते खरीदने की आवश्यकता है। बॉक्स बनाने के लिए कितने गत्तो की आवश्यकता है?
questions.explanation:
**Given: **

Length (l) = 12 inches, 

Breadth (b) = 8 inches, 

Height (h) = 10 inches 

**Formula used:** 

Surface area cuboid = 2 (lb + bh + lh) 

**Calculation:** 

The amount of cardboard needed to build the box:  

⇒ 2 × [(12 × 8) + (8 × 10) + (12 × 10)] 

⇒ 2 × [96 + 80 + 120] 

⇒ 2 × 296 = 592 sq. inches.

**∴ The total amount of cardboard needed to build the box is 592 sq. inches.**

questions.explanation:
**Given**

Marked prices and discounts for articles A, B, C, D, and E.

**Concept:** Selling price = Marked price - Discount

**Solution:**

⇒ Calculate the selling price for each article by subtracting the discount from the marked price.

⇒ Sum the selling prices of all articles for L2.

⇒ Calculate the average discount of articles C and D for L1.

⇒ L1 = (Discount of C + Discount of D)/2 = (66 + 72)/2 = 69

⇒ L2 = (A's SP + B's SP + C's SP + D's SP + E's SP) = [(350 - 70) + (650 - 75) + (450 - 66) + (750 - 72) + (850 - 80)] = 280 + 575 + 384 + 678 + 770 = 2687

L2 + L1 = 2687 + 69 = 2756

**Therefore, the values of L2 + L1 is 2756.**

A, B, C, D, और E के लिए अंकित मूल्य और छूट। 

**अवधारणा: **विक्रय मूल्य = अंकित मूल्य - छूट

**हल:**

⇒ अंकित मूल्य से छूट मूल्य को घटाकर प्रत्येक वस्तु के विक्रय मूल्य की गणना करते हैं।

⇒ L1 के लिए वस्तु C और D पर औसत छूट की गणना करते हैं।

⇒ L1 = (C पर छूट + D पर छूट)/2 = (66 + 72)/2 = 69

⇒ L2 = (A का SP + B का SP + C का SP + D का SP + E का SP) = [(350 - 70) + (650 - 75) + (450 - 66) + (750 - 72) + (850 - 80)] = 280 + 575 + 384 + 678 + 770 = 2687

यहाँ, SP = विक्रय मूल्य 

L2 + L1 = 2687 + 69 = 2756

**इसलिए, L2 + L1 का मान 2756 है।**
